criteria.text: Rate-limit error/event shape captured verbatim in the baseline doc, or a documented simulation strategy recorded if a real limit could not be triggered safely.

citations.quotedAssertion: THE FIRST DISJUNCT, satisfied — the shape captured VERBATIM, four distinct payloads. :356 '{"status":"allowed","resetsAt":1784135400,"rateLimitType":"five_hour","overageStatus":"rejected","overageDisabledReason":"org_level_disabled","isUsingOverage":false}' and the three `allowed_warning` siblings at :357 (utilization 0.96), :358 (0.98) and :359 (0.99), each carrying 'surpassedThreshold':0.9. The envelope shape is at :350 '{"type":"rate_limit_event","rate_limit_info":{...},"uuid":"<uuid>","session_id":"<uuid>"}'. :347 names the four committed transcript fixtures these were read out of, so the quotes are anchored to files, not to memory.

THE SECOND DISJUNCT, also satisfied — the documented reason no real limit was triggered, and the finding that made triggering unnecessary: :343 '**No dedicated live trigger was run** — the owner's subscription (the same account every spike authenticates as) hit a session limit earlier on 2026-07-15 before this phase began, and mid-phase the limit was hit AGAIN, interrupting this phase's own fix round; deliberately exhausting it further was and remains unsafe. However, a validation-round audit found that **the structured signal shape did not need triggering: it was already captured incidentally** — the SDK streams `rate_limit_event` messages during ordinary, non-limited operation, and this phase's own committed transcripts contain **16 of them**.'

THE SIMULATION STRATEGY ITSELF, for the one variant the verbatim capture does not cover: :378 '- **MITIGATION:** the next time any worker naturally hits a limit while streaming, capture the raw message sequence verbatim into `spikes/fixtures/07-ratelimit.live-capture.sanitized.jsonl` and update the `ratelimit.exhausted-variant-shape` verdict. Never trigger deliberately on the owner's subscription; a dedicated/metered test account or off-hours window is the only acceptable deliberate path. Until captured, phase 13 must treat the `'rejected'`-transition handling as built on the SDK's _typed_ promise, exercised only against fake-engine fixtures, and phase 06 must ALSO detect the error-string channel (sentence naming the limit kind + localized reset time) as a fallback signal, since that is how an actual exhaustion has been observed to surface.' This is the recorded strategy the criterion's second disjunct asks for: opportunistic capture, an explicit no-deliberate-trigger rule, a named acceptable path, and a directive for what downstream phases may build on meanwhile.

The one exhausted-limit sample that DOES exist, recorded verbatim in the error-string channel rather than the structured one: :374 opens 'Every committed event carries `status` `'allowed'` or `'allowed_warning'`; a live `'rejected'` sample — and whatever terminal result/error message accompanies an actually-refused request in-stream — has not been captured', and :376 gives it as '> `Agent terminated early due to an API error: You've hit your session limit · resets 2:10pm (Europe/Madrid)`'. So even the un-captured variant is documented by the one real observation available, not left blank.

criteria.notes: The criterion is a DISJUNCTION — "captured verbatim in the baseline doc, OR a documented simulation strategy recorded if a real limit could not be triggered safely" — and this pass verified BOTH halves hold rather than picking whichever was easier. Half one: four distinct `rate_limit_info` payloads are quoted verbatim in §8 (:356-359) across 16 committed samples in four named transcript fixtures. Half two: :343 documents why no deliberate trigger was run (the owner's own subscription; it had already been exhausted twice during the phase) and :378 records the resulting strategy in full. Satisfying a disjunction twice over is worth stating explicitly because the two halves cover DIFFERENT variants: the verbatim capture covers `allowed`/`allowed_warning`, and the strategy covers the `rejected`/exhausted variant that has never been observed in-stream. Neither half alone would cover the criterion's whole subject, which is exactly why the doc has both. On the safety judgement itself: not triggering was the right call and remains binding — `packages/engine-claude/src/live/live-harness.ts:623` implements it in code by ABORTING the live suite on a `rejected` status rather than recording it.

criteria.notes: Conjunctive, and the second conjunct is a repo-wide NEGATIVE claim, so it was censused by NOTATION rather than by one grep — the brief's own hardest-won lesson, since a grep that cannot express a second notation returns a SMALLER answer with no error and reads as clean. CONJUNCT 1 holds on both readings: the literal `UNRESOLVED:` form occurs exactly once (:372, mitigation :378), and on the broad reading there are four UNRESOLVED items in the document (§5 :268, §8 :372, §9's trigger-safety id, §18.2 :685) and four mitigation notes (:270, :378, :343+:378, :694). CONJUNCT 2 IS CLEAN: 20 notations swept over the whole tracked tree, 46 candidate files intersected and read, 44 code-side `'rejected'`-shape lines classified one by one; every site is explicitly hedged as SDK-typed, hand-built, unobserved-live, fake-engine-only, or not-probe-verified. TWO SITES DO BETTER THAN HEDGING IN PROSE and are why this is recorded as clean rather than merely un-violated: `rate-limit-fixtures.test.ts:21` makes the prohibition an executable assertion, and `live-harness.ts:623` inverts the polarity by ABORTING the live suite on a `rejected` status. TWO NITS, reported because a bucket labelled clean must not hide anything: `e2e/matrix/orchestration/test/limit-parked-resume-restart.test.ts:194` builds a `rejected` payload for the FAKE engine — which is precisely what :378's mitigation prescribes, so it is compliant — but lacks the one-line comment its sibling `packages/scheduler/src/run-driver.test.ts:456-459` carries; and `docs/evidence/phase-06/wi2-event-normalizer.md:141-142` still describes the pre-Finding-6 injection scope that `event-normalizer.ts:75-79` reversed, which misstates the injection scope rather than any UNRESOLVED status. Both are filed as a defect record; neither changes this classification. Had either been a genuine reliance on an UNRESOLVED fact as settled, conjunct 2 would be UNMET and this box would stay unticked — that was the pre-agreed handling and it did not have to be used.
